Crucially the existing audit cannot see it: apps/web/src/lib/a11y/theme-tokens.ts:97-101 `readThemes` parses only app/globals.css, so apps/web/src/lib/a11y/contrast.test.ts audits declared tokens and is structurally blind to any hex written inside a component. There is no lint rule or test anywhere under apps/web enforcing token-only colour (eslint.config.mjs has no such rule).
tenancy.smallest_real_change: Replace the literal at TenureAIPanel.tsx:121 with the token (`color="var(--primary)"`, i.e. drop the prop). Then add apps/web/src/lib/a11y/no-raw-color.ts exporting a pure `findRawColors(source: string, filename: string): { line: number; value: string }[]` that flags hex literals, `rgb(`/`hsl(` literals and Tailwind arbitrary colour classes (`text-[#…]`, `bg-[#…]`) outside comments, and a test no-raw-color.test.ts that walks `src/components/**` and `src/app/(app)/**` with fs.readdirSync and asserts the list is empty, with an explicit allowlist for the three legitimate document-root cases already in the tree (app/layout.tsx:37-38 viewport theme-colour meta, app/manifest.ts:15-16, app/apple-icon.tsx:23 — none of which can reference a CSS var). This mirrors the existing theme-tokens.ts approach of reading the real files rather than a hand-kept copy. Mutation to prove it bites = restore `color="#25a96d"`, the sweep test fails naming that file and line. The requirement's first clause (re-anchoring the ramp at #0F3D2E; today `--primary: #198052`, app/globals.css:37) is a deliberate design decision that would re-open the GE-022-003 contrast audit and should not be changed without the TTES Bible's calibrated ramp in hand.

tenancy.title: Light and dark canvases are not the art-directed palettes the requirement names, and nothing prohibits the failure modes it lists
tenancy.why_open: apps/web/src/app/globals.css:53-55 sets the light canvas to `#f0efe9`/`#fbfaf7`/`#ebeae3` — a warm cream (blue channel lowest), not the required soft cool-neutral. Lines 194-197 set the dark canvas to `#08090a`/`#0f1113`/`#15181c` — a neutral near-black, not a green-charcoal. apps/web/src/lib/a11y/theme-tokens.ts already parses these blocks out of the real stylesheet for four themes, and apps/web/src/lib/a11y/contrast.test.ts asserts only contrast ratios: there is no assertion that a canvas is never effectively pure white or pure black, that the dark palette is not an algorithmic inversion of the light one, that accents are not neon, or that adjacent greys clear a minimum separation. So both halves of the requirement — the art direction and the prohibitions — are unimplemented, and this is checkable without a database.
tenancy.smallest_real_change: Add `apps/web/src/lib/a11y/canvas-policy.ts` with pure predicates over the token maps `theme-tokens.ts` already returns: `isPureExtreme(hex)` (luminance above/below a named threshold), `isAlgorithmicInversion(lightTokens, darkTokens)` (each dark canvas token is within tolerance of 255-minus the light one), `isNeon(hex)` (HSL saturation over a named ceiling at high lightness), and `greyOnGreySeparation(a, b)`. Add `canvas-policy.test.ts` running all four themes through them. Then retune the two canvas ramps in globals.css so light is cool-neutral (blue channel >= red) and dark is green-charcoal (green channel highest, base luminance lifted off pure black), keeping every existing contrast assertion green. Mutation: set `--bg-base` in the dark block to `#000000` and the pure-extreme test fails; set the dark canvas to the exact inverse of the light one and the inversion test fails.

tenancy.title: Validate status tokens for colour-vision differentiation, low-brightness legibility and display gamut
tenancy.why_open: The token set the requirement names does exist in `apps/web/src/app/globals.css` (canvas/surface/elevated at lines 53-55, text 74-76, border 65-68, action 38-41, focus 68, and the four status families `--success` 86, `--warning` 89, `--error` 92, `--info` 95, plus dark-mode counterparts at 212-223). What does not exist is any validation beyond WCAG ratio: `apps/web/src/lib/a11y/contrast.ts` (174 lines) is sRGB→luminance→ratio only, and `grep -rin "deuteran|protan|tritan|gamut|colou?r.vision" apps/web/src` matches nothing but the word "luminance" inside that same file. The audit at `apps/web/src/lib/a11y/contrast.test.ts` therefore passes a palette in which `--success #1c8c5a`, `--warning #b07a10` and `--error #c2402a` are the classic red/green/amber confusion triple — each individually contrast-compliant against the surface, and mutually indistinguishable to a deuteranope, which is exactly the failure the requirement separates from contrast.
tenancy.smallest_real_change: Add `apps/web/src/lib/a11y/colour-vision.ts` with a Brettel/Viénot LMS simulation (`simulate(rgb, "deuteranopia"|"protanopia"|"tritanopia")`) and a perceptual distance (CIE76 ΔE over sRGB→XYZ→Lab), reusing `parseColor`/`composite` from `contrast.ts` so translucent dark-mode `-light` tokens are composited first. Add an audit test in the established pattern — read the real four themes via `readThemes(GLOBALS_CSS)` and assert every pair drawn from {success, warning, error, info} stays above a stated ΔE floor under each simulation, and that each status token also clears a low-brightness floor (luminance-halved surface) and sits inside sRGB. It fails red the moment someone edits `globals.css` into an indistinguishable palette, which is what makes it load-bearing. Mutation proof: set `--warning` to `#1c8c5a` in a temp copy of the stylesheet (the file-path parameter `readThemes` already accepts, as `contrast.test.ts` line 11-13 already does with `os.tmpdir()`) — the differentiation assertion must fail while every existing contrast assertion still passes.

tenancy.title: Tenant accent must not override focus, status or the high-contrast palette, and must be contrast-validated or refused with an explanation
tenancy.why_open: apps/web/src/app/(app)/layout.tsx:70,74 injects `brandingCss(...)` as a `<style>` inside <body>. packages/platform-config/src/branding.ts:123-145 builds that block as `:root{--primary: <tenant hex>; --primary-hover: ...; --primary-text: ...}` after validating ONLY the hex SHAPE (branding.ts:27-29). Three consequences the requirement forbids are all present: (1) `--primary` IS the focus indicator — apps/web/src/app/globals.css:350 `[data-focus-visible] { outline: 2px solid var(--primary) }` and :481 for chart hit targets — so a tenant colour changes focus meaning; (2) globals.css:369-381 raises the accent to `#0f6b42` under `@media (prefers-contrast: more) { :root { --primary: ... } }`, same specificity as the injected `:root` but EARLIER in document order (stylesheet in <head>, tenant block in <body>), so a tenant hex silently defeats an accessibility override; (3) nothing computes contrast — any hex is accepted against the unchanged `--primary-text: #ffffff`, with no adjust-or-reject path and no explanation returned. The repo already ships the maths (`contrastRatio`, `meetsAA`, `AA_THRESHOLD` in apps/web/src/lib/a11y/contrast.ts) and a live parse of the real palette (apps/web/src/lib/a11y/theme-tokens.ts); branding.ts uses neither. Registry FAIL, no ledger entry.
tenancy.smallest_real_change: Add `apps/web/src/lib/branding/accent-guard.ts` exporting `governAccent(branding)` -> `{ branding, adjustments: {token, from, to, reason}[], refusals: {token, value, reason}[] }`. Using the existing `contrastRatio`/`AA_THRESHOLD` from lib/a11y/contrast.ts and the real light/dark/high-contrast palettes from lib/a11y/theme-tokens.ts it (a) darkens the accent in fixed steps until it clears 4.5:1 against the tenant's `primaryTextColor` and 3:1 against `--bg-surface` in BOTH themes, refusing with a reason when no step clears; (b) refuses an accent within a contrast-equivalence threshold of the reserved `--error`/`--success`/`--warning`/`--info` fills so a tenant identity colour cannot read as a status. Then in layout.tsx call `governAccent` before `brandingCss` and wrap the emitted block in `@media not (prefers-contrast: more){...}` so the accessibility override always wins. Mutation to prove the test: drop the `@media not (prefers-contrast: more)` wrapper and assert the emitted CSS no longer preserves `#0f6b42`; separately feed `#ffffff` with white text and assert a refusal with a reason, then delete the contrast gate and confirm red. Boundary note: `brandingCss` lives in packages/platform-config — this change does not need to edit it, the guard runs at the injection point inside apps/web.

tenancy.title: Theme supports only light/dark/system — no scheduled theme, and forced-colors / high-contrast platform behaviour is not honoured
tenancy.why_open: apps/web/src/components/ThemeSwitcher.tsx:8-12 declares exactly three options and persists a single 'tenure-theme' string; there is no schedule concept anywhere. The pre-hydration script at apps/web/src/app/layout.tsx:46 (injected at :65) resolves only dark | system | light, so even if a schedule were stored it would flash the wrong theme on first paint — which is the specific failure the requirement forbids. `grep -n 'forced-colors' apps/web/src/app/globals.css` returns zero hits; the file has `prefers-contrast: more` at :370 and `prefers-reduced-motion` at :400 but nothing for Windows High Contrast / forced-colors, so the token-driven palette (apps/web/src/lib/a11y/theme-tokens.ts) silently overrides the user's system colours on every surface, border and focus ring.
tenancy.smallest_real_change: New pure module apps/web/src/lib/a11y/theme-schedule.ts exporting `resolveTheme(pref, { nowMinutes, darkFromMinutes, darkUntilMinutes, systemPrefersDark })` returning 'light' | 'dark', handling the midnight-wrap window (e.g. 20:00 -> 07:00) and falling back to `systemPrefersDark` for pref 'system'. Add a fourth 'Scheduled' radio to ThemeSwitcher.tsx writing 'tenure-theme-schedule' alongside 'tenure-theme'. Generate the layout.tsx:46 init string from the SAME resolution rule (export the body as a string constant from the module and interpolate it) so the pre-paint answer cannot drift from the runtime one — that is what keeps 'without wrong-theme flash' true. Add a `@media (forced-colors: active)` block to globals.css setting the token custom properties to system keywords (Canvas/CanvasText/LinkText/Highlight) and `forced-color-adjust: none` only where a token must survive. Tests in theme-schedule.test.ts: inside window -> dark; outside -> light; wrap-around window at 23:59 and 06:59; boundary minutes inclusive/exclusive; 'system' ignores the window; and an equivalence test asserting the exported init-string body and `resolveTheme` agree across a table of inputs. Mutation: flip the wrap-around branch — the 23:59 and 06:59 cases fail, and the equivalence test fails too.

tenancy.title: No governed comfortable/compact density — one fixed density, no preference, nothing holding the 4px grid
tenancy.why_open: Grepping `density` across apps/web/src and packages returns nothing at all. apps/web/src/app/globals.css:131-140 defines a correct 4px scale (--space-1 4px through --space-16 64px) but there is exactly one set of values; globals.css:142 comments the frame as 'compact / ERP-dense' as a fixed choice, not a mode. apps/web/src/components/ThemeSwitcher.tsx is the only appearance preference in the product and covers light/dark only. So neither density exists, nothing lets a user choose, and nothing asserts that a density keeps type readable, touch targets accessible or values on the grid.
tenancy.smallest_real_change: Define the two densities as `:root[data-density="comfortable"]` / `[data-density="compact"]` overrides of the --space-* and control-height tokens in globals.css, every value a multiple of 4px and every interactive height >= 44px. Ship a DensitySwitcher modelled on ThemeSwitcher (persisted the same way, stamped on documentElement) and render it next to it. Add apps/web/src/lib/a11y/density.ts that parses both density blocks out of globals.css using the existing brace-balanced reader in apps/web/src/lib/a11y/theme-tokens.ts, and a test asserting for BOTH densities: every space token is a multiple of 4, every control-height token is >= 44px, and body type does not drop below the readable floor. Test needs no database. Mutation proof: set a compact control height to 36px, or a space token to 6px, and the corresponding assertion must fail.

tenancy.title: The document-save conflict pattern is advisory — the optimistic check is read-then-write, so concurrent autosaves lose data silently
tenancy.why_open: apps/web/src/app/api/documents/[id]/save/route.ts:84 compares `doc.updatedAt.toISOString()` against `payload.baseUpdatedAt` and 409s, but `doc` was read at :48 (`db.document.findUnique`) outside any transaction, S3 is overwritten at :113 BEFORE any database write, and the write at :118 is `db.document.update({ where: { id: doc.id } })` with no `updatedAt` predicate. Two autosaves that read the same baseline — which the debounced client at apps/web/src/components/documents/DocumentViewerOverlay.tsx:235 makes routine — both pass :84, both upload, and the second silently wins with neither client told there was a conflict. The header comment at :18 claims 'Optimistic-locked on updatedAt', so the claim is what is wrong.
tenancy.smallest_real_change: Claim the version before touching S3: replace the :118 update with `db.document.updateMany({ where: { id: doc.id, updatedAt: doc.updatedAt }, data: { version: { increment: 1 }, sizeBytes: bytes.length } })`, return the 409 when `count === 0`, and only then call `uploadDocument`; re-read `updatedAt` for the response. Extract the decision into a pure `resolveSaveClaim({ storedUpdatedAt, baseUpdatedAt, claimedRows })` in apps/web/src/lib/documents/save-claim.ts returning 'conflict' | 'proceed' | 'bad_request', and unit-test it. Mutation: make resolveSaveClaim ignore `claimedRows` (return 'proceed' whenever the strings matched) -> the 'second concurrent writer with a stale row claim is a conflict' test fails; restore -> passes.

tenancy.title: Standardize destructive and cross-organization previews with exact target, scope, affected count, downstream effects, and recovery window

tenancy.title: File upload controls: sniff real type, refuse active content and polyglots, checksum, safe delivery

Registry has `ledger: null` for GE-063-004 and the id appears nowhere in the global-engine ledger, so nothing claims it done.
other.smallest_real_change: Add `sequence: number` and `previousHash: string | null` to `AuditRecordInput`/`AuditRecord` and compute a `recordHash` over the frozen record in `buildAuditRecord` (record.ts:196) using the same node:crypto sha256 the releases package already uses. New `verify.ts` exporting `verifyChain(records)` -> `{ok, tampered: {sequence, expectedHash, actualHash}[], gaps: {after, before, missing}[]}` (gap = a break in the per-tenant sequence, which is precisely what an append-only log cannot otherwise reveal) and `projectForQuery(records, {sensitivity})` that re-applies `redactMetadata` on read so an export cannot leak what the write redacted. New `retention.ts` exporting `applyRetention(records, {retainDays, asOf}, holds: LegalHold[])` returning `{expire, retain, heldBack}` where a record matching any active hold is NEVER in `expire`. All pure functions over arrays — no database, so this is fully doable on this host. Mutation test that proves it: make `applyRetention` ignore the holds array and assert the 'a record under legal hold is never expired' test fails; separately flip one byte of a record's metadata and assert `verifyChain` reports it tampered. CROSS-AREA: the chain only becomes real once the two production writers persist `sequence`/`previousHash` — apps/web/src/lib/admin/guard.ts:2 and apps/web/src/lib/provisioning/reconcile.ts:1 both call `buildAuditRecord`. Keep the new fields optional at first so those call sites keep compiling, and report the persistence step as the cross-area dependency it is.

other.title: Audit administrators cannot rewrite integrity-root evidence
other.why_open: There is no integrity root. packages/audit/src/record.ts is 211 lines with no hash, chain, digest, sequence number or anchor of any kind — `AuditRecord` (lines 73-87) is tenantId/actor/action/resource/outcome/reason/metadata/traceId/occurredAt and nothing else, and packages/audit/src/index.ts exports only the builder and the redactor. Both real callers (apps/web/src/lib/admin/guard.ts:70 and apps/web/src/lib/provisioning/reconcile.ts:368) write those fields straight into `db.auditEvent.create`, so an UPDATE against the AuditEvent row by anyone holding write access leaves no trace and nothing anywhere can detect it. The requirement is to *prove* the rewrite is refused; today nothing can even notice it.
other.smallest_real_change: Compute a content digest inside `buildAuditRecord` over the canonical, post-redaction record and place it, plus the digest of the caller-supplied predecessor, into the namespaced metadata keys the builder already uses for provenance (`_digest`, `_prev`, alongside the existing `_releaseId` / `_policyDecision` at record.ts:191-194). That lands in real storage with no schema change and no caller edit, because both callers persist `record.metadata`. Export `verifyAuditChain(records)` returning the first record whose recomputed digest or predecessor link disagrees. Test: build a three-record chain, mutate the middle record's `action`, assert `verifyAuditChain` names that record; mutation = have the digest cover only `occurredAt`, the test then passes the tampered chain and fails. Be honest in the doc comment about the limit: an in-row digest detects a partial edit and a chain detects a single-row rewrite, but a writer who rewrites every subsequent row still wins until the head is anchored outside the database. Cross-area dependency, not to be fixed here: anchoring the chain head (a periodic head digest written to the control plane or object storage with Object Lock) needs apps/web and infrastructure/terraform.

other.title: Workflow definitions have states/transitions/guards but no start triggers, domain events, schedules, webhooks or manual starts

other.title: Document save is a read-then-write, so a replay or a concurrent save applies twice instead of conflicting
other.why_open: `apps/web/src/app/api/documents/[id]/save/route.ts:84-86` compares `doc.updatedAt.toISOString()` (read at :48) against `payload.baseUpdatedAt` and returns 409 on mismatch, then at :118-121 issues an unconditional `db.document.update({ where: { id } , data: { version: { increment: 1 } } })`. The check and the write are separate statements against a row nothing locks, so two requests carrying the same `baseUpdatedAt` — a retry from the editor's autosave, or two tabs — both pass :84, both overwrite S3 at :113, both increment `version`, and both write a `Document.Edited` audit row at :123. That is two effects from a replayed request and a stale write that overwrites rather than conflicting. The route has a real caller (`apps/web/src/components/documents/DocumentViewerOverlay.tsx:200`). The idempotency+optimistic-concurrency primitive already exists in `apps/web/src/lib/commands/bus.ts:117-216` and has no production caller at all — `grep -rn "commands/bus" apps/web/src` matches only the module and its own test.

Mutation: swap `updateMany` back to `update({ where: { id } })` and the test reports two successes.

other.title: Tenant branding cannot violate minimum contrast, phishing-resistant login identity, or accessible focus/status tokens
